did_you_know.text: Did you know? Psalm 119 opens by declaring blessed are those who walk according to the Lord’s law, presenting the Torah as a way of life.
Did you know? The psalm explicitly asks how a young person can keep their way pure and answers: by keeping the word of the Lord.
Did you know? The psalmist describes storing the word of the Lord in one’s heart as a means of helping a person avoid sin.
Did you know? The psalmist asks, “Open my eyes, that I may behold wondrous things from your Torah”—that is, he views deep understanding of the Torah as a gift that requires prayer.
Did you know? Even in times of despair and danger, the psalmist turns to the word of the Lord as a source of life and strength.
Did you know? The psalmist declares that the Torah from the Lord’s mouth is better for him than thousands of pieces of gold and silver, placing its spiritual value above material wealth.
Did you know? The psalm says that the word of the Lord stands firm forever in heaven, emphasizing its stability and eternity.
Did you know? The verse “Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path” presents the word of the Lord as a light guiding a person along life’s way.
Did you know? The psalmist says, “Seven times a day I praise you,” expressing the high frequency of his thanksgiving for the Lord’s righteous judgments.
Did you know? The psalm ends with the image of the psalmist as a lost sheep: he asks the Lord to seek his servant, even though he himself declares that he has not forgotten the Lord’s commandments.
